accounting.rationale: The source uses should, not shall, for the decimal exponent range of a stat-variable. It records a portability recommendation because a processor-dependent error code might otherwise not be representable; no conformance requirement or diagnostic obligation is created here.
The source recommends, but does not require, a decimal exponent range of at least four for a stat-variable.
The representability concern explains the recommendation for stat-variable range; processor-dependent code selection is not turned into a portable executable oracle.

This paragraph scopes the rest of 9.7.4 to ALLOCATE or DEALLOCATE statements that contain a STAT= alloc-opt or dealloc-opt. The statement syntax is owned by 9.7.1.1 and 9.7.3.1, so this unit is structural rather than a separate testable requirement.
The unit identifies when the STAT= semantics in this subclause apply; it does not add a distinct syntax or execution effect beyond the following paragraphs.
ALLOCATE alloc-opt syntax is owned by 9.7.1.1 and DEALLOCATE dealloc-opt syntax by 9.7.3.1; this catalogue only accounts for their shared STAT= semantics.

The unnumbered note points to ALLOCATED and ASSOCIATED as ways to check object status after unsuccessful allocation or deallocation. The intrinsic functions are owned elsewhere and the normative status effects are accounted in p6.
The note is advisory and does not add a conformance requirement beyond the p6 object-status semantics.

requirements.title: A STAT variable is a scalar integer variable
requirements.definition: The grammar for stat-variable is scalar-int-variable. A STAT= specifier in an ALLOCATE or DEALLOCATE statement therefore designates a scalar integer variable; scalarity, integer type, and variable status are all required by this rule. Image-selector-specific exclusions for STAT targets are owned by 9.6, not by this ALLOCATE/DEALLOCATE subclause.

pending.scalar-integer-stat-variable: PENDING positive source plan: execute ALLOCATE(x, STAT=s) for an unallocated INTEGER allocatable scalar x and scalar INTEGER variable s initialized to -77; after successful execution observe s==0, ALLOCATED(x), and an independent literal assigned to x. The STAT form is material because ERRMSG and other options are absent.
pending.nonscalar-stat-variable-rejected: PENDING diagnostic/control source: attempt ALLOCATE(x, STAT=s) where s is a rank-one INTEGER array in an otherwise valid allocation; repair only to a scalar INTEGER variable and observe STAT zero plus an allocated-object literal. Invalidity is attributable to R946 scalar-int-variable, not to ALLOCATE syntax.
pending.noninteger-stat-variable-rejected: PENDING diagnostic/control source: attempt ALLOCATE(x, STAT=r) where r is a scalar REAL variable in an otherwise valid allocation; repair only to a scalar INTEGER variable and observe STAT zero plus an allocated-object literal. Invalidity is attributable to R946 integer type.
pending.nonvariable-stat-expr-rejected: PENDING diagnostic/control source: attempt ALLOCATE(x, STAT=0) or STAT=(s+0) with all allocation operands otherwise valid; repair only to STAT=s where s is a scalar INTEGER variable and observe STAT zero plus an allocated-object literal. Invalidity is attributable to R946 variable status.

requirements.title: A STAT variable is independent of allocation actions, allocate-object properties, and ERRMSG value
requirements.definition: The stat-variable shall not itself be allocated or deallocated within the ALLOCATE or DEALLOCATE statement in which it appears. Its denotation shall not depend on the value, bounds, deferred type parameters, allocation status, or association status of any allocate-object in that statement, and shall not depend on the value of the errmsg-variable. These are real restrictions on the statement semantics, but because they are unnumbered execution-time dependence restrictions this catalogue does not invent a blanket static diagnostic duty.

pending.stat-variable-not-allocate-object: PENDING diagnostic-policy/control source: attempt ALLOCATE(s, STAT=s) where s is an unallocated INTEGER allocatable scalar and all other syntax is valid; repair by using a separate scalar INTEGER status variable st and observe st==0, ALLOCATED(s), and assigned literal 401. Invalidity is attributable to S9.7.4-001 rather than R946, because s is otherwise a scalar integer variable.
pending.stat-variable-not-deallocate-object: PENDING diagnostic-policy/control source: allocate scalar INTEGER allocatable s first, then attempt DEALLOCATE(s, STAT=s); repair by using separate scalar INTEGER st and observe st==0 and ALLOCATED(s)==.FALSE. Invalidity is attributed to the p3 prohibition on deallocating the stat-variable in the same statement, not to DEALLOCATE syntax.
pending.no-stat-value-dependence-on-allocate-obj: PENDING diagnostic-policy/control source: use a stat-variable designator such as st(f(x)) where f references the current value of allocate-object x in the same ALLOCATE or DEALLOCATE statement and all indices are otherwise valid; repair by computing the index from an independent literal before the statement and observe STAT zero plus allocated/deallocated status. No read of an undefined or unallocated x value is proposed.
pending.no-stat-bounds-dependence-on-allocate-ob: PENDING diagnostic-policy/control source: select STAT=st(UBOUND(a,1)) or an equivalent scalar integer variable designator whose subscript depends on the bounds of allocate-object a in the same statement; repair by using an independent literal subscript and observe STAT zero plus a literal object value. Runtime detectability is limited and no required static diagnostic is claimed.
pending.no-stat-deferred-type-parameter-dependen: PENDING diagnostic-policy/control source: make the STAT variable designator depend on LEN or another deferred type parameter of a same-statement character or parameterized allocate-object; repair by using a prior independent length value and observe STAT zero plus LEN/literal. Attribution excludes type-parameter declaration rules.
pending.no-stat-allocation-status-dependence-on-: PENDING diagnostic-policy/control source: select the STAT variable using MERGE or an index expression dependent on ALLOCATED(a) for an allocatable allocate-object a in the same statement; repair by evaluating the inquiry before the statement into an independent variable and observe STAT zero and allocated/deallocated status. The plan treats ALLOCATED itself as owned by 16.9.13.
pending.no-stat-association-status-dependence-on: PENDING diagnostic-policy/control source: select the STAT variable using ASSOCIATED(p) for pointer allocate-object p in the same statement; repair by evaluating the inquiry before the statement into an independent variable and observe STAT zero and ASSOCIATED(p). The plan never calls ASSOCIATED on an undefined association status.
pending.no-stat-errmsg-value-dependence: PENDING diagnostic-policy/control source: use a STAT variable designator whose subscript depends on LEN_TRIM(msg) or another value of the ERRMSG variable in the same statement; repair by using an independent literal subscript and observe STAT zero plus the successful allocation or deallocation sentinel. Invalidity is attributed to S9.7.4-001, not to R931/R946 variable form.

requirements.title: Successful ALLOCATE or DEALLOCATE with STAT defines the STAT variable as zero
requirements.definition: Successful execution of an ALLOCATE or DEALLOCATE statement that has an applicable STAT= specifier causes the stat-variable to become defined with the value zero. The zero value applies on success; p5 supplies the values for stopped-image, failed-image, and other error conditions.

pending.allocate-success-defines-stat: PENDING complete source: initialize scalar INTEGER s=-501, execute ALLOCATE(x, STAT=s) for an unallocated allocatable scalar x, then read s only after the statement and observe s==0, ALLOCATED(x), and assigned literal 501. The prior sentinel proves s was defined by the statement.
pending.allocate-success-stat-zero: PENDING complete source: allocate an allocatable array with independent bounds and STAT=s, then observe s==0, SIZE/LBOUND/UBOUND, and literal element values. No allocation failure is induced or used as an oracle.
pending.deallocate-success-defines-stat: PENDING complete source: allocate scalar x successfully first, set s=-503, execute DEALLOCATE(x, STAT=s), then observe s==0 and ALLOCATED(x)==.FALSE. The deallocation success path is material.
pending.deallocate-success-stat-zero: PENDING complete source: allocate two independent allocatable objects, deallocate both with STAT=s, and observe s==0 plus both ALLOCATED inquiries false. DEALLOCATE syntax and deallocation semantics remain 9.7.3 dependencies.

requirements.title: STAT values distinguish stopped images, failed images without other errors, and other errors
requirements.definition: For an ALLOCATE statement with a coarray allocate-object, or a DEALLOCATE statement with an allocate-object that is a coarray or has a coarray potential subobject component, execution when the current team contains a stopped image defines stat-variable with STAT_STOPPED_IMAGE from ISO_FORTRAN_ENV. Otherwise, if such a statement is executed when the current team contains a failed image and no other error condition occurs, stat-variable is defined with STAT_FAILED_IMAGE from ISO_FORTRAN_ENV. If any other error condition occurs during ALLOCATE or DEALLOCATE execution, stat-variable is defined with a processor-dependent positive integer value different from STAT_STOPPED_IMAGE and STAT_FAILED_IMAGE.

pending.coarray-allocate-stopped-image-stat-stop: PENDING multi-image source plan requiring at least two images and a separately gated stopped-image capability: execute an ALLOCATE of a coarray allocate-object with STAT=s in a current team that contains a stopped image, then observe s==STAT_STOPPED_IMAGE imported from ISO_FORTRAN_ENV and a reached literal sentinel on an active image. The stopped image is not fabricated and no failed-image value is accepted for this facet.
pending.coarray-deallocate-stopped-image-stat-st: PENDING multi-image source plan requiring at least two images and a separately gated stopped-image capability: after establishing a coarray or coarray-potential-subobject allocate-object, execute DEALLOCATE(..., STAT=s) while the current team contains a stopped image and observe s==STAT_STOPPED_IMAGE plus an active-image sentinel. DEALLOCATE object syntax and coarray potential subobject classification are dependencies.
pending.stopped-image-precedes-failed-image: PENDING multi-image source plan requiring at least two images and a separately gated environment that can distinguish stopped and failed images in the current team. If a conforming harness can create both conditions for an applicable coarray ALLOCATE or DEALLOCATE, the oracle is STAT_STOPPED_IMAGE rather than STAT_FAILED_IMAGE. This facet is blocked until the suite has a safe, standard-conforming way to create the premise; no failed or stopped image is fabricated.
pending.failed-image-no-other-error-stat-failed: PENDING multi-image source plan requiring at least two images and a separately gated failed-image capability: execute an otherwise successful coarray ALLOCATE or qualifying DEALLOCATE when the current team contains a failed image and no other error occurs, then observe s==STAT_FAILED_IMAGE imported from ISO_FORTRAN_ENV. The plan must also establish that syntax, allocation status, and bounds do not introduce another error.
pending.other-allocate-error-positive-distinct-s: PENDING non-resource runtime source plan: create a deterministic standard-specified ALLOCATE error such as allocating an already allocated allocatable object with STAT=s and ISO_FORTRAN_ENV constants in scope; observe only the portable properties s>0 and s different from STAT_STOPPED_IMAGE and STAT_FAILED_IMAGE, with a repaired control that deallocates first and observes s==0 plus literal 505. This is a deterministic standard error condition rather than a resource failure, and it must not deliberately exhaust memory.
pending.other-deallocate-error-positive-distinct: PENDING non-resource runtime source plan: execute DEALLOCATE on a known-unallocated allocatable object, the deterministic standard-specified error condition from 9.7.3.2 p1, with STAT=s and ISO_FORTRAN_ENV constants in scope; observe only the portable properties s>0 and s distinct from STAT_STOPPED_IMAGE and STAT_FAILED_IMAGE, with a repaired control that allocates first then deallocates and observes s==0. This is not a resource-exhaustion oracle.
pending.no-resource-exhaustion-stat-oracle: PENDING source-classification guard: any future STAT nonzero allocation or deallocation case for this requirement must use a deterministic standard-specified non-resource error condition owned by 9.7.1.2, 9.7.1.3, or 9.7.3, or a separately gated stopped/failed image premise. Deliberately exhausting memory, oversizing an allocation, or fabricating a stopped or failed image is explicitly not an acceptable oracle.

requirements.title: Object status after STAT_FAILED_IMAGE and other STAT errors follows the specified success or retention rules
requirements.definition: If stat-variable became defined with STAT_FAILED_IMAGE, each allocate-object is successfully allocated or deallocated on all active images of the current team. If any other error condition occurs, each allocate-object has a processor-dependent status, subject to three guarantees: an object successfully allocated has allocation status allocated or pointer association status associated; an object successfully deallocated has allocation status unallocated or pointer association status disassociated; and an object not successfully allocated or deallocated retains its previous allocation status or pointer association status.

pending.stat-failed-image-active-allocate-succes: PENDING multi-image source plan requiring at least two images and a separately gated failed-image capability: execute a coarray ALLOCATE that yields STAT_FAILED_IMAGE and no other error, then on each active image observe the local allocate-object allocated with expected bounds and an independent literal assignment. The failed image is not queried and the STAT_FAILED_IMAGE value is not fabricated.
pending.stat-failed-image-active-deallocate-succ: PENDING multi-image source plan requiring at least two images and a separately gated failed-image capability: establish a qualifying coarray or coarray-potential-subobject allocate-object on active images, execute DEALLOCATE that yields STAT_FAILED_IMAGE and no other error, then observe the active-image local allocation status unallocated or pointer status disassociated. Multi-image execution is separately gated.
pending.other-error-status-processor-dependent: PENDING non-resource runtime source plan: use a mixed ALLOCATE or DEALLOCATE statement with one deterministic standard-specified non-resource error, such as a previously allocated allocatable object in an ALLOCATE list or a known-unallocated allocatable object in a DEALLOCATE list, and observe the nonzero STAT from S9.7.4-003 plus only the three p6 bullet guarantees for each object. The oracle records allowed per-object statuses, not a processor-independent order or which objects the processor chose to process.
pending.successfully-allocated-object-has-succes: PENDING conditional source plan: in a multi-object ALLOCATE with a deterministic standard-specified non-resource error and SOURCE literals, if an independent object is observed allocated or a pointer object associated after nonzero STAT, verify only the p6 bullet guarantee that a successfully allocated object has allocation status allocated or pointer association status associated. The facet cannot guarantee observation on every processor because p6 makes the per-object status processor dependent after other errors.
pending.successfully-deallocated-object-has-succ: PENDING conditional source plan: in a multi-object DEALLOCATE with a deterministic standard-specified non-resource error, if an independent object known allocated or associated before the statement is observed unallocated or disassociated after nonzero STAT, record only the p6 bullet guarantee that a successfully deallocated object has allocation status unallocated or pointer association status disassociated. The plan must not require a processor to deallocate that object before detecting the other error.
pending.unsuccessful-allocatable-retains-status: PENDING non-resource runtime source plan: include an object whose allocation or deallocation is known not to be successful under a deterministic standard-specified error, such as an already allocated allocatable in an ALLOCATE error or a known-unallocated allocatable in a DEALLOCATE error, and observe after nonzero STAT only the p6 bullet guarantee that the unsuccessful object retains its previous allocation status. No undefined or deallocated value is read.
pending.unsuccessful-pointer-retains-association: PENDING non-resource runtime source plan: use a pointer allocate-object with defined association status in an ALLOCATE or DEALLOCATE statement that encounters a separate deterministic standard-specified error, then observe with ASSOCIATED only when the pointer association status is defined that an unsuccessfully allocated or deallocated pointer retains its previous association status. The plan must avoid ASSOCIATED on undefined pointer status and cannot rely on address comparison.
